policy.rule: A functional item is PASS only when repository evidence plus the exact-head CI run directly proves the declared behavior. Source-code presence alone is not sufficient for browser/Figma runtime behavior.

capture.reason: The Standard adapter contract is tested, but CI does not yet execute a real browser deterministic online/current-document capture fixture.
No exact-head automated browser test currently proves successful file:// capture after explicit extension file-access permission.

LocalFolderProvider tests prove document-relative/root-relative resolution, missing-resource reporting, traversal blocking and remote-reference separation; the source-providers test suite passed in CI #745.
Region geometry, clipping, exclusions and precision are tested, but the current suite does not directly prove end-to-end capture keeps every intersecting node plus required structural ancestors.
Scroll evidence exists in the capture contract, but no browser fixture currently exercises both document and primary application scroll-root semantics end to end.
The adapter contract requires shadowRoot and assignedNodes and the Class B source fixture exists, but no measured browser capture artifact has yet proven the composed-tree result.
contentDocument support is guarded by tests and a source fixture exists, but no measured browser capture artifact has yet proven the nested document result.
The STANDARD_CAPTURE_FRAME_INACCESSIBLE contract is present, but no browser cross-origin fixture currently proves the diagnostic/fallback behavior.
No automated runtime artifact currently proves capture freezes the current visual state and restores the page without permanent mutation.
No automated runtime artifact currently proves page scroll, focus and temporary styles are restored through finally-equivalent cleanup after success and failure.

packageAcceptance.reason: Packager tests prove deterministic .wtf ZIP bytes, manifest/checksums, required payload paths, traversal rejection and canonical JSON; schema tests passed in the exact-head quality chain.
Parser hostile-fixture tests pass and the UI performs parseWtfPackage before enabling renderer handoff.
Pixel Ground Truth infrastructure exists, but this audit has not yet produced a package-level fixture proving each declared capture profile includes exactly the required pixel reference payload.

importAcceptance.reason: The choose-file event path and intake descriptor are implemented, but no DOM-level UI interaction test currently exercises the complete choose flow.
Canvas drop intake is implemented, but no Figma-runtime integration test currently exercises an actual drop event through secure parse and render.
The UI disables import until parseWtfPackage succeeds, parser hostile fixtures pass, and renderer handoff consumes only currentParsed validated content.
The renderer creates W2F_IMPORTING_ROOT_NAME, marks transactionState importing, then commits after the plan is applied; the behavior is covered by tests.
Injected adapter mutation failure proves the temporary root is removed; the plugin also removes renderedRoot if later hybrid/visual/layout stages fail.
Renderer tests prove semantic names are preserved and blank names receive deterministic useful fallback names.
Tests prove stable source IDs, revision hashes, source tag/selector and document/revision identities are persisted in pluginData.
Capability resolver tests prove native/wrapper/absolute/emulated/raster/unsupported decisions and stable reasons; renderer pluginData preserves render strategy metadata.
Section defaults/normalization and selected-root subtree rendering are directly covered by tests.
Commit calls adapter.setSelection([root]) and adapter.focusNodes([root]); tests assert both calls and the Figma adapter maps them to currentPage.selection and viewport.scrollAndZoomIntoView.

fontAcceptance.reason: resolveFont implements exact family/style preference, but there is no independent automated font-resolution test yet.
Same-family/default fallback is implemented and fontFallbackCount exists, but the audit has not yet proven a user-visible diagnostic distinguishes substitution from an exact match.
Correction is an allowed strategy, not currently established as a tested end-to-end font fallback behavior.
No dedicated policy test currently proves text cannot be rasterized solely to hide missing-font/substitution errors.
